extracted.intended_audience: early-career biomedical researchers preparing K99/R00 career-development and research proposals (and NIH reviewers/staff evaluating them)
extracted.subtask_description: Drafting the candidate information, career development, mentorship, specific aims, research strategy, timelines, benchmarks, and methodological details for an NIH K99/R00 (biomedical) grant application.

rubrics_metrics.name: Advisory/mentoring committee composition and meeting frequency
rubrics_metrics.description: I have designed a scientific advisory panel including experts in diverse fields within the San Francisco Bay Area. I will work directly with the members of these labs, and have committee meetings every 6-9 months during the K99 phase. We will work on my scientific progress, career development, and future publication and grant applications.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include a diverse panel of experts relevant to the proposal, schedule regular committee meetings (here: every 6-9 months during K99), and use meetings to review scientific progress, career development, and grant/publication plans.

rubrics_metrics.name: Hands-on in-laboratory training with named experts (durations specified)
rubrics_metrics.description: In depth in-laboratory training will occur in both labs: I will spend a full month in the Eisen lab working with Drs. Xiao-Yong Li and Colleen Hannon to learn how to perform and analyze ChIP-seq and ATAC-seq. I will train in the Ting lab for 3-6 weeks to troubleshoot and develop a miniTurbo method for C. elegans.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specify concrete in-lab training rotations with mentors, list the techniques to be learned, and give approximate durations to demonstrate feasibility and mentorship commitment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Regular mentor interactions and presentation schedule
rubrics_metrics.description: I will participate in all Drubin lab meetings and present my own data every 3-6 months ... I will also meet with Dr. Drubin every month ... I will meet with Dr. Brunet every 2-3 months, and present in her lab meeting for critical feedback at least every 6 months.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Define frequencies for one-on-one meetings and lab presentations (e.g., monthly meetings; present data every 3–6 months) to show ongoing mentorship and feedback.

rubrics_metrics.name: Career training: teaching and mentoring responsibility
rubrics_metrics.description: Within the Dillin lab, I will continue to mentor high school, undergraduate, and graduate students, and technicians and postdocs. I will also continue working with Dr. Dillin in his molecular genetics lab in designing and carrying out a laboratory course to increase my capacity to be an efficient educator.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include concrete teaching/mentoring tasks (mentoring students, designing/carrying out a course) as part of the career development plan to develop pedagogical skills.

rubrics_metrics.name: Commitment to increasing diversity in STEM
rubrics_metrics.description: A large goal of mine is to increase the diversity – both of underrepresented minorities and underrepresented socioeconomic groups – in STEM. Currently, I am part of the B2B program at UC Berkeley and the CHORI/CIRM summer research programs. I plan to actively work with the heads of these programs to increase my involvement and how to incorporate these types of programs into my future institute.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Describe existing involvement and concrete plans to expand participation in diversity programs; articulate how this will be integrated into future roles.

rubrics_metrics.name: Lab management training
rubrics_metrics.description: I am expanding my expertise in lab management by working with our exceptional lab manager, Larry Joe, as he teaches me how to manage finances, personnel, and inventory of a lab. Moreover, he allows me to engage in direct negotiations with vendors.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include hands-on training in budgeting, personnel management, inventory control, and vendor negotiation as part of career preparation for running an independent lab.

rubrics_metrics.name: Writing and grant-writing development
rubrics_metrics.description: I will continue to write future manuscripts independently, with Dr. Dillin’s input to refine and hone my writing skills. I have also written multiple grants ... I will continue to expand my writing skills by co-authoring future R01 and R21-level grants.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Present a plan for manuscript and grant-writing practice, including co-authoring with mentors and taking lead on progress reports and grant drafts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Detailed timeline with explicit career and research benchmarks
rubrics_metrics.description: Timelines for Career Benchmarks ... K99 year 1 ... K99 year 2 ... R00 year 1 ... R00 year 2 ... R00 year 3 ... Benchmark Goals: Revisions for papers ... Complete, write, and submit paper ... Finalize scWB techniques ... Submit R00 transition proposal ... Acquire faculty position offer ... Recruit personnel: hire technician, recruit undergraduate and graduate students.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide a multi-year timeline (K99 and R00 phases) with specific milestones (manuscripts, technique finalization, R00 submission, faculty applications, hiring) tied to dates/periods to demonstrate realistic planning and progression to independence.

rubrics_metrics.name: Concrete benchmark goals and deliverables
rubrics_metrics.description: Benchmark Goals include: submit revisions for papers on non autonomous UPRER and TMEM’s role; Complete and submit paper characterizing lysosome role in ER quality control; Finalize scWB techniques on quantifying F:G actin ratios; Troubleshoot proximity labeling in C. elegans; Submit application packet for multiple faculty positions; Recruit personnel; Write and submit methods/resource paper on proximity labeling.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: List precise deliverables (papers, methods, troubleshooting milestones, grant submissions, hiring) mapped to the timeline to allow assessment of progress.

rubrics_metrics.name: Well-defined specific aims with hypotheses and tissue specificity
rubrics_metrics.description: Aim 1: How does chromatin remodeling and lipid homeostasis regulate actin organization and function? Aim 2: Building biochemical tools to study cytoskeletal form and function during aging. Aims include specific sub-questions about tissue specificity and lifespan regulation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: State clear, focused aims with testable hypotheses and specify the biological scope (e.g., tissue specificity, aging) to frame experiments and evaluation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of multiple complementary screening approaches and cross-validation
rubrics_metrics.description: We have performed multi-pronged genetic screening ... in vivo live cell imaging of actin, synthetic lethality screening, transcriptome analysis, and whole genome CRISPR-Cas9 screening ... Cross-referencing these rich datasets has revealed two critical nodes of genes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Design studies using orthogonal/complementary methods and cross-reference results across datasets to increase confidence in candidate hits.

rubrics_metrics.name: Development and adaptation of novel experimental tools
rubrics_metrics.description: I created LifeAct-mRuby transgenic lines for tissue-specific visualization of F-actin, are developing single cell western blot (scWB) protocols to quantify F:G actin ratios, and will employ proximity labeling with miniTurbo/TurboID for actin interactome identification.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Describe creation/adaptation of technical tools with rationale and preliminary demonstration of their utility; propose how new tools will enable the proposed aims.

rubrics_metrics.name: Pre-specified sample sizes, independent replicates, and statistical tests
rubrics_metrics.description: Filament structure measured in vivo (n > 50 animals per condition; >2 independent trials using 3 aging methods for >6 total replicates). For thickness measurements n > 30 animals per condition; integrated intensity n > 500 animals per condition; FRAP n > 30 animals per condition ... For 1-4, >3 independent trials per experiment with Mann-Whitney statistical testing. Lifespans & thermotolerance on >120 adult animals per condition; >3 independent trials; log-rank testing for significance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide explicit n per condition, number of independent trials, and the planned statistical test for each assay to justify power and analysis plans.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of multiple, orthogonal quantitative and qualitative assays
rubrics_metrics.description: Quantitative/qualitative measures include: 1) thickness of muscle actin filaments (n > 30); 2) integrated fluorescent intensity of actin via COPAS large particle biosorter; 3) indirect measurement of intestinal F-actin using ratio of LifeAct in filaments vs. cytoplasm (n > 500); and 4) dynamics of actin using FRAP (n > 30; statistics run on t=1/2 measurements).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Measure phenotypes with several independent assays (morphology, intensity, ratios, dynamics) to ensure robust and convergent evidence.

rubrics_metrics.name: Validation of knockdown phenotypes in genetic nulls
rubrics_metrics.description: All knockdown experiments will be validated in null mutants synthesized by CRISPR-Cas9-mediated gene editing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Confirm RNAi/knockdown results using genetic null alleles (CRISPR/Cas9-generated) to rule out off-target or partial-effect explanations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of multiple aging paradigms to ensure robustness
rubrics_metrics.description: Animals are aged using the following methods: 1) adults washed off plates and eggs/progeny aspirated away; 2) chemical sterilization with FUDR; 3) adults manually picked away from progeny. (>2 independent trials using 3 aging methods for >6 total replicates.)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Perform aging experiments across several established aging methods to ensure results are not an artifact of a single handling protocol.

rubrics_metrics.name: Experimental replication across independent trials
rubrics_metrics.description: For assays 1-4, >3 independent trials per experiment ... lifespans & thermotolerance on >120 adult animals per condition; >3 independent trials.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Plan multiple independent experimental replicates to assess reproducibility and permit appropriate statistical analyses.

rubrics_metrics.name: Pre-planned caveats and alternative strategies
rubrics_metrics.description: CAVEAT 1: if bet-1 overexpression does not extend lifespan, experiments can be done in bet-1 knockdown or lof animals ... CAVEAT 2: it is possible that massive overexpression of bet-1 may be toxic, and thus titrating bet-1 levels may be necessary ... experiments: 1) single-copy overexpression using mosSCI; 2) tissue-specific overexpression; 3) overexpression of specific isoforms.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Anticipate potential negative outcomes and specify alternative experimental routes (e.g., different genetic manipulations, expression levels, tissue-specific approaches) to rescue aims and interpret results.

rubrics_metrics.name: Mechanistic dependency/epistasis testing
rubrics_metrics.description: I will treat bet-1 overexpressing strains with RNAi targeting actin and known actin-regulating genes, such as tropomyosins, the ARP2/3 complex, and formins, to determine whether loss of broad and specific actin regulatory genes is sufficient to attenuate the lifespan extension found in bet-1 overexpressing animals.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Design experiments that test whether phenotypic effects (e.g., lifespan extension) are dependent on the proposed pathway/component by perturbing downstream or interacting factors.

rubrics_metrics.name: Personnel, hiring, and lab setup plan for transition to independence
rubrics_metrics.description: R00 year 1: Lab set up and secure staff ... Recruit personnel: hire technician, recruit undergraduate and graduate students ... Manage teaching requirements ... Begin thesis projects for students.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide a concrete hiring and lab-setup plan for the independent phase (R00), including personnel types/timelines and initial training/teaching responsibilities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Dissemination and diversified funding strategy
rubrics_metrics.description: Plan to write and submit methods/resource papers on proximity labeling; submit smaller grants (e.g. NSF, Glenn/AFAR, ASA, etc.); Submit R21 on riskier project; Submit R01 on cross communication between ER and cytoskeletal quality control.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include an explicit publication plan and parallel/subsequent grant strategies across multiple funders to support research continuity and growth.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of preliminary data to demonstrate feasibility
rubrics_metrics.description: Preliminary data: I have created a system to interrogate cytoskeletal quality in vivo in C. elegans ... performed the first comprehensive analysis of changes to actin filaments during aging ... obtained the first direct evidence that actin structure and integrity decline during late adulthood in multiple tissue types.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Present clear preliminary results that demonstrate feasibility of key approaches and support the central hypotheses; leverage prior tools and initial findings to justify proposed work.
